subject: Deployment mode + migration follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@aurora-health.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@aurora-health.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up & next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks again for the demo and the candid discussion this morning — really appreciated the context on Aurora's mix of OpenAI usage and your in-house Triton cluster. Quick recap and proposed next steps.

Recap (from our call):
- Current setup: OpenAI for burst/innovation + legacy Triton cluster for high-volume batch inference.
- Key constraints: want ~<200ms p95 for real-time flows, expect peak ~200 req/min but with spiky bursts during end-of-day processing.
- Compliance: must meet HIPAA requirements and prefer US-only data residency.
- Migration driver: reduce per-token costs, improve latency predictability, and consolidate observability across workloads.

Redwood deployment options we discussed (short):
- Hosted API: fastest to get started, pay-as-you-go, Redwood handles keys & infra. Good for dev/low sensitivity workloads.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools + predictable throughput, autoscaling, burst capacity. Strong candidate for your mixed throughput needs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed networking, HSM/KMS, full control — recommended if PHI workflows must never touch a third-party control plane.

Questions to help us recommend a concrete plan (please reply inline):
1) Can you confirm target p95 latency requirement for the customer-facing real-time path? (you mentioned <200ms)
2) Typical request payload size (tokens) for real-time vs batch jobs?
3) Any strict blackout windows or maintenance windows we should avoid for migration?
4) Who should we loop for a technical deep-dive (Dev? Infra?) — happy to schedule a 60-min session next week.

Attached: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft timelines & responsibilities).

Next steps: if you confirm the bullets above, I’ll put together a recommended deployment blueprint (Dedicated vs Private) + a rough cost/throughput estimate and availability windows.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
[Attachment: mutual-action-plan.xlsx]

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@aurora-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aurora-health.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up & next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Answers inline: 

1) Latency: yes, our SLO target is p95 <200ms for the patient-facing realtime endpoints. For background batch jobs we can tolerate higher latencies (1-2s).
2) Payload sizes: realtime payloads average ~120 tokens in, 80 tokens out. Batch jobs are larger (avg 2k tokens per request) processed in bulk.
3) Maintenance: we have weekly maintenance windows Saturdays 02:00–04:00 PT; avoid major migrations in that window.
4) Loop in: Samir (infra lead) and our security lead if/when we talk about Private/VPC. For the tech deep-dive, Samir and I will join.

Notes on current infra: we use OpenAI for most conversational flows and a self-hosted Triton cluster for batched model runs. The Triton cluster is on-prem and behind our VPN. We’re evaluating a move off OpenAI for cost predictability but want to keep peak capacity and HIPAA controls.

Attached: aurora-llm-architecture-diagram.png (high-level).

-Alex
Alex Chen
Director of AI Engineering | Aurora Health
alex.chen@aurora-health.com
[Attachment: aurora-llm-architecture-diagram.png]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aurora-health.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up & next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Great — this is exactly the level of detail we needed, thanks. Quick take:

- Recommendation: start with Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for your mixed workload. Dedicated gives predictable p95 latency and cost controls, plus burst capacity for end-of-day batches.
- Private VPC: recommended only if you require the control plane to be customer-managed (HIPAA with strict on-prem constraints). We can support Private VPC with HSM/KMS and offline connectivity, but that adds setup time vs Dedicated.
- Hosted API: good fallback for non-PHI/dev traffic and rapid proof-of-concept.

Technical call: Dev (cc’d) should be able to walk through integration patterns (KV caching, token batching, and autoscaling policies). Dev — can you confirm availability for a 60-min session next week?

I’m attaching our Dedicated pricing summary so you have a starting point for procurement discussions. If you’re comfortable, I can also draft an initial MSA outline and a 90-day migration plan that minimizes downtime (incremental traffic shift + live A/B).

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf]
